ai.literal: deceitful / he of the mind / deceitful / conduct / elements / all five / inside-indeed / will laugh
ai.translation: The five elements within his own body will laugh inwardly at the hypocritical conduct of a man with a deceitful mind.
ai.modern: வஞ்சகமான மனத்தை உடையவனின் பொய்யான ஒழுக்கத்தைக் கண்டு, அவனது உடம்பில் உள்ள ஐம்பூதங்களும் தமக்குள்ளே சிரிக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet exposes the folly of hypocrisy by pointing out that a person cannot hide their true nature from themselves. The 'five elements' (earth, water, fire, air, space) that make up the person's own body are constant witnesses to their deceit. Even if the world is fooled by their outward conduct, their own inner being will mock their false behavior. The word 'நகும்' (will laugh) powerfully personifies the elements, showing the absurdity of trying to fake virtue.

ai.literal: Sky-high appearance what will do, one's own heart oneself knowing fault if incurs.
ai.translation: What good is a sky-high appearance of holiness, if one's own heart secretly commits a fault it knows to be wrong?
ai.modern: தன் நெஞ்சம் தவறு என்று அறிந்த ஒரு குற்றத்தை ஒருவன் செய்தால், அவனது வானளாவிய உயர்ந்த தோற்றத்தால் என்ன பயன்?
ai.explanation: This couplet questions the value of outward displays of greatness or asceticism when contradicted by inner guilt. The phrase 'sky-high appearance' refers to a grand, saintly exterior that commands respect. However, if a person commits a fault that their own conscience recognizes as wrong, that outward show becomes completely worthless. True conduct requires the mind to be as pure as the outward appearance suggests.

ai.literal: Without strength, he of [such] nature [taking a] strong appearance, [is like a] cow, of tiger skin having covered, having grazed, like that.
ai.translation: A man of weak nature taking on a mighty ascetic appearance is like a cow grazing while covered in a tiger's skin.
ai.modern: மன அடக்கம் இல்லாதவன் துறவிக்குரிய வலிமையான தோற்றத்தைக் கொண்டிருப்பது, ஒரு பசு புலியின் தோலைப் போர்த்திக்கொண்டு பயிரை மேய்ந்ததைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a striking simile to expose the hypocrisy of false ascetics. A person who lacks the inner strength to control their senses but wears the impressive garb of a renunciant is compared to a cow wearing a tiger's skin. Just as the cow uses the terrifying disguise of a tiger to graze safely on others' crops without being chased away, the false ascetic uses the respected appearance of a holy man to indulge in worldly pleasures without being questioned. The contrast between the weak nature ('வலியில் நிலைமையான்') and the strong appearance ('வல்லுருவம்') perfectly mirrors the harmless cow hiding beneath the fierce tiger's skin.

ai.literal: Hiding behind asceticism doing wrong things is like a hunter hiding behind a bush having trapped a bird.
ai.translation: Committing evil deeds while hiding behind the guise of asceticism is like a hunter hiding behind a bush to snare a bird.
ai.modern: தவக்கோலத்தில் மறைந்து கொண்டு தீய செயல்களைச் செய்வது, ஒரு வேடன் புதரின் பின்னால் மறைந்து கொண்டு பறவையைப் பிடிப்பதைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet exposes the hypocrisy of false ascetics. It compares a person who uses the holy appearance of a sage to commit wicked deeds to a hunter who uses a bush for camouflage. Just as the hunter hides to deceive and trap an innocent bird, the false ascetic uses a pious disguise to deceive and exploit others. The powerful imagery highlights the predatory nature of such deceitful conduct.

ai.literal: Attachment we are without, those who say, deceitful conduct, what what saying, sorrow many will give.
ai.translation: The deceitful conduct of those who claim to be free from attachments will bring them many sorrows, making them cry out, 'What have we done? What have we done?'
ai.modern: பற்றுக்களை விட்டுவிட்டோம் என்று சொல்லிக்கொண்டு வாழ்பவர்களின் வஞ்சகமான நடத்தை, ஐயோ இப்படிச் செய்துவிட்டோமே என்று அவர்கள் வருந்தும்படியான பல துன்பங்களைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the hypocrisy of ascetics who claim to have renounced all worldly attachments but secretly engage in deceitful behavior. The phrase 'what, what' (எற்று எற்று) vividly captures the bitter regret they will eventually feel. Their false conduct will inevitably lead to numerous sorrows, forcing them to lament their own actions.

ai.literal: In heart they do not renounce, like those who renounced having deceived, than those who live, hard-hearted people there are none.
ai.translation: There are no people more hard-hearted than those who live deceitfully, pretending to be ascetics while not truly renouncing desires in their hearts.
ai.modern: மனத்தால் பற்றுக்களை விடாமல், விட்டவர்களைப் போல உலகத்தை ஏமாற்றி வாழ்பவர்களை விடக் கொடியவர்கள் யாருமில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet condemns the hypocrisy of false ascetics. The phrase neñciṉ tuṟavār describes those who have not genuinely given up worldly attachments in their minds. Yet, they deceive others by living tuṟantārpōl, meaning like true renunciates. The poet declares that there are no people more cruel or hard-hearted (vaṉkaṇār) than such hypocrites, because they exploit the trust and reverence society places in genuine ascetics.

ai.translation: The world has people who look as fair as the kunri seed on the outside, but are as black as its tip on the inside.
ai.modern: வெளியில் குன்றிமணியைப் போலச் சிவப்பாகவும் அழகாகவும் காணப்பட்டாலும், உள்ளத்தில் அந்தக் குன்றிமணியின் மூக்கைப் போலக் கருமையான எண்ணம் கொண்டவர்களை இவ்வுலகம் கொண்டுள்ளது.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses the image of the kunri seed, which is bright red but has a black tip. It compares hypocrites to this seed. On the outside, they appear pure and virtuous, but on the inside, their minds are dark with deceit. The word 'uṭaittu' implies that the world unfortunately contains such deceptive people.

ai.literal: That of the mind impurity being, glorious people water having bathed, having hidden behaving people are many.
ai.translation: There are many people who harbor impurity in their minds, yet bathe in water to appear like the pure, hiding their true conduct.
ai.modern: தங்கள் மனத்திற்குள் அழுக்கை வைத்துக்கொண்டு, வெளியில் சிறந்தவர்களைப் போல நீரில் குளித்துத் தங்கள் உண்மையான இயல்பை மறைத்து வாழும் மனிதர்கள் உலகில் பலர் உள்ளனர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet exposes the hypocrisy of those who focus on outward purity while remaining inwardly corrupt. The phrase 'manattatu macu aka' describes the mind retaining its stain or impurity. Meanwhile, 'mantar nir ati' shows them bathing in water to imitate truly glorious or pure people. By doing so, they hide their true nature ('maraintu oluku'), and the poet notes that such deceitful people are numerous ('mantar palar').

ai.literal: Arrow is cruel, lute curve is good; thus like that, by the nature resulting from action, understand.
ai.translation: An arrow is straight but cruel, while a lute is curved but sweet. In the same way, judge people by the nature of their deeds, not their appearance.
ai.modern: கணை நேராக இருந்தாலும் கொடியது, யாழின் வளைவு கோணலாக இருந்தாலும் இனிமையானது. அதுபோலவே மக்களின் தோற்றத்தை வைத்து அல்லாமல் அவர்கள் செய்யும் செயல்களின் தன்மையை வைத்து அவர்களைப் புரிந்துகொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet teaches that outward appearance does not reveal true character. An arrow is perfectly straight but brings harm, whereas the curved neck of a lute produces sweet music. Therefore, one must judge people by the nature of their actions rather than their physical form or outward guise. The word 'koṭitu' means cruel or crooked, contrasting with 'cevvitu' which means upright or good. The poet plays on the visual straightness of the arrow and the physical curve of the lute to show that true straightness lies in good deeds.

ai.literal: Shaving and lengthening are not needed, world that which is condemned having abandoned if one leaves.
ai.translation: There is no need to shave the head or grow matted hair, if one simply abandons the conduct that the world condemns.
ai.modern: உலகம் பழிக்கும் தீய செயல்களை ஒருவன் முழுமையாக விட்டுவிட்டால், அவன் துறவியாகத் தலைமுடியை மழிப்பதோ அல்லது சடாமுடியாக நீளமாக வளர்ப்பதோ தேவையில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet addresses the outward signs of asceticism, such as shaving the head bare or growing long, matted hair. It states that these physical transformations are completely unnecessary for true virtue. The only requirement is to abandon behaviors and actions that the world condemns as wrong. By focusing on inner purity and rejecting blameworthy conduct, a person achieves true discipline without needing external costumes or rituals.
